method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: SvelteKit runtime, the app shell, and the reader item chunk every day view shares - item cards, the in-place topic filter and the per-day read mark.

/<date>/.why: The same runtime, shell and reader item chunk as /, on one day's items.

/<date>/<topic>/.why: The same runtime, shell and reader item chunk as /, on one topic of one day.

/404.why: Runtime and app shell and nothing route-specific. This is the floor every other route sits on.

/archive/.why: Runtime and shell plus the archive route, which now lists stories instead of dates: the month-index fetch and decode, the newest-first regrouping, the paged list and its Show-more control, and the encoder guard it already carried. What the bytes buy is a page that stops growing with every published story - it fetches one month at a time instead of inlining the corpus. Derived, not pasted: an untouched origin/main build on this tree read /archive/ at 44,543 B and the changed one at 45,708 B, so the change is +1,165 B and 44,554 + 1,165 is what CI should see. A local Windows build reads 10 to 73 B under CI's Linux npm ci on every route, which is why the delta is the measurement and the absolute is not.

/console/.why: Runtime and shell plus the console route: hand-written SVG charts and the d3-scale and d3-array arithmetic behind them, the stage-timing decade axis with its minor stubs and its gap-instead-of-plunge run splitting, the Charts table that says what the router cost and what it published on each day, and now the What the model did table - nine counts of the day's own items, the divider row that names a model change, and the dash, percent and whole-unit formatters that keep a raw score off the screen. That section cost +1,196 B: the same tree measured 64,962 B with the four console files at origin/main and model-work.ts absent, and 66,158 B with them, on one machine on 2026-08-26.

/evals/.why: Runtime and shell plus the stub that moves an old bookmark to /console/.
